title: Test helper child.exitCode ?? 0 reads a Bun.spawnSync failure as exit 0, so a broken spawn can pass green
description:
Reported by team-lead 2026-10-14, from a qcli353 failure seen while validating QCLI-445.

The shared spawn helper in the test tree reads the child exit code as `child.exitCode ?? 0`. When Bun.spawnSync FAILS to spawn (resource exhaustion, EAGAIN/ENOMEM, common under the parallel full-suite run), `child.exitCode` is null and the `?? 0` reports exit 0. A test asserting a command FAILED then sees a pass-shaped 0 and reports a confusing mismatch -- qcli353 saw exit 0 with empty stderr where exit 2 and a message were expected -- and a test asserting success would read the failed spawn as success. Silent, and it turns test infrastructure failure into a wrong verdict rather than a loud error.

Scope: 37 occurrences across 35 files under test/ (grep -rn "exitCode ??" test/). TYPE: test-only, not production -- src/adapters/migration/jira/importer.ts:191 uses `process.exitCode ?? 1`, which fails closed and is NOT this defect (confirmed 2026-10-14).

Representative line: test/qcli353-flag-shaped-positional.test.ts:26.

Fix direction: do not fold a null exit code into 0. Default to a non-zero (or assert the spawn succeeded) so a spawn failure fails the test loudly instead of masquerading as an exit code.

Ruling: queue this AFTER the sweep-split task (QCLI-501).

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every test-tree site that reads a spawned child exit code treats a null exitCode, or a spawn error, as a loud failure naming the command and the spawn error -- never a pass-shaped 0. A single shared helper is preferred over 37 hand edits.
A test proves it both ways: a spawn that cannot start (a nonexistent executable is enough) fails loudly, and a normal exit-0 child still passes.
A mutation check: restoring child.exitCode ?? 0 in the helper makes the new test go red. The result is recorded on the task.
Production code is out of scope: src/adapters/migration/jira/importer.ts:191 is left alone and the PR says so.
The full suite is green; any flake is reported, with its test name.

plan: 1. Add a shared spawn helper that fails loudly on a null exit code or a spawn error, naming the command.
2. Migrate all 37 test-tree sites to it (one shared helper, not 37 different fixes).
3. Prove both ways: a spawn that cannot start fails loudly; a normal exit-0 child passes; plus a signal-killed child.
4. Mutation check: restore ?? 0 and confirm the new test goes red.
5. Full suite; report any flake by name. PR leaves production code alone.
finalSummary:
QCLI-502: the test tree's spawn helpers no longer fold a null exit code into 0.

WHAT CHANGED. test/helpers/spawn.ts exports runCommand(argv, {cwd, env, stdin}) -- the single place that turns a spawned child into an exit code. It throws, naming the command and the cause, when the spawn cannot start (Bun throws ENOENT) or when exitCode is null (a signal-terminated child); a normal exit, zero or non-zero, is returned unchanged. All 37 sites across 35 files that read child.exitCode ?? 0 now delegate to it -- a script-assisted migration over an identical return block, then verified by typecheck and the affected suites.

WHY. child.exitCode is null for a signal-killed child (SIGKILL under memory pressure, an AMFI kill): verified, exitCode null with signalCode SIGKILL. The ?? 0 fold made that a pass-shaped 0, so a test asserting a command FAILED could pass, and a test asserting success could read a dead child as success.

PROVED BOTH WAYS. test/qcli502-spawn-failure-fails-loud.test.ts, 3/3: a spawn that cannot start fails loudly naming the command; a SIGKILLed child fails loudly instead of reporting exitCode 0; a normal exit-0 and a normal non-zero exit (7) are returned as-is.

MUTATION CHECK, RUN AND RECORDED. Restoring child.exitCode ?? 0 in the helper makes the SIGKILL test go RED -- it received {exitCode: 0} where it expects a throw. Restored afterwards; no residue.

PRODUCTION OUT OF SCOPE. src/adapters/migration/jira/importer.ts:191 uses process.exitCode ?? 1, which fails closed, and was left alone.

VERIFIED. typecheck, lint and format:check clean. New suite 3/3; a 7-file smoke slice of the trickiest migrations 33/33; full suite 1207 pass / 1 fail. The single failure is the local-only QCLI-411 check, which its own test says must run on the pinned runtime (package.json pins bun 1.4.2 and this machine has 1.3.14) -- red by design locally, green on CI. No other flake and no timeout observed.
